steps.decide: Whether this is a menu of actions or a select of values, because they are different widgets
How the trigger, the list and the keyboard contract relate
Where the menu renders when the trigger sits near a viewport edge
How destructive items are separated and confirmed
How async items load and what the trigger says meanwhile

rules.statement: A menu holds actions and closes on activation; a select holds values and keeps its chosen value visible in the trigger. Using one for the other breaks the keyboard contract either way.
Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu with focus on the first item; arrows cycle, Home and End jump, typeahead matches, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
The menu flips and shifts to stay inside the viewport, and never renders off-screen behind a scroll container; a menu taller than its space scrolls internally.
Destructive items sit below a separator, are labelled with the object they affect, and require confirmation; they are never the item under the pointer when the menu opens.
Async items show a pending row inside the open menu, the trigger keeps its label while loading, and a failed load offers retry inside the menu rather than closing it.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: an open menu owns its request; a response for a menu that has closed is dropped, and a response for a superseded query is discarded by sequence

motion.motion: the menu fades and offsets into place over 140ms
motion.reducedMotion: the menu appears instantly in place

transitions.trigger: an item is chosen or Escape is pressed

motion.reducedMotion: the menu disappears instantly and focus returns to the trigger

motion.motion: a pending row appears inside the menu over 120ms
the list fades in over 140ms without resizing the menu twice
motion.reducedMotion: the list appears instantly at its final height

motion.motion: a retry row replaces the pending row over 120ms
the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.motion: the control returns to pending over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the control returns to pending instantly

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Expose a small set of actions or values from one trigger without hiding them behind a second navigation level.
useCases: choose a status from five values
nicheDifferences: A dropdown is cheap to open and expensive to get wrong: focus, placement and closing behaviour are the whole widget
The difference between menu and select is not cosmetic, it is what Enter does
inputs: whether the items are actions or values
the trigger's context near viewport edges
anatomy: a trigger with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded
a listbox or menu with roving focus
a pending and a retry row
styling: the menu sits 4 px below the trigger with one shadow level
items are 40 px tall with the keyboard shortcut right-aligned
destructive items use the danger colour only inside the menu
a11y: role=menu/menuitem or role=listbox/option, never a div soup
the trigger reflects expanded state and the menu is labelled by the trigger
Escape closes and restores focus, and focus never moves to the body
disabled items are skipped by arrow navigation and expose their reason
responsive: the menu narrows to the trigger width but never below 180 px
at 320 px the menu becomes a bottom sheet with the same keyboard contract
placement flips above the trigger when there is no room below
copy: shortcuts are shown as text, not only as symbols
an empty menu says why there is nothing to do
alternatives: inline buttons when the actions are two and always visible
a select with a search field (combobox) when the value list is long
a context menu for canvas-style surfaces
acceptance: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu onto the first item
Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger
the menu stays inside the viewport near edges and scrolls internally when tall
destructive items are separated, object-named and confirmed
a failed async load offers retry without closing the menu
failureCases: focus escapes to the document body when the menu closes
the menu opens off-screen at the right edge of a scrolled table
Delete sits under the pointer and fires on a double click
the select's trigger loses the chosen value after selection

refused.reason: individual items disable; the trigger itself is either available or removed
a select's own options are static; async loading belongs to a combobox, not a select
